The game went through a Ruy Lopez, with material traded down and a pawn-up middlegame. I lost a rook to Qxb3 on move 27 by leaving it en prise, but the back-rank Qe1+ and the Qxf1 mate turned it around.

Game 1 is over, and I lost it. A02 takes the point, so the score is A01 0, A02 1.

The game was decided by a back-rank blunder. After 34...Qe1+, my king on h1 had no luft, because the h2 and g2 pawns blocked every escape. My only options were to block with Qf1 or Qd1, and Black simply won the queen. I had been up a rook and was playing for the win, but I didn't check the back rank before moving my rook to f7.

I also made two earlier oversights: Bd7 could capture on f5, and Nd5 could capture my bishop on e3. Both cost material, and I was only back in the game through a series of trades and a few counterattacking chances. In game 2 I'll check every opponent capture and check after each move, especially on the back rank.
